subject: Biology
title: The Tundra
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Tundra usable.

hook.text: The tundra is the coldest biome on Earth—temperatures can plunge below minus 40 degrees.

buildup.text: Permafrost—permanently frozen ground—sits just below the surface, preventing tree growth.

discovery.text: Despite the cold, mosses, lichens, and hardy shrubs survive, along with caribou and arctic foxes.

twist.text: Thawing permafrost releases methane—a greenhouse gas 80 times more potent than CO₂ short-term.

climax.text: The tundra stores twice as much carbon as the atmosphere. Its thaw could accelerate warming.

punchline.text: The frozen ground holds a climate time bomb.

quiz.question: What is permafrost?
options: Permanently frozen ground below the surface
A layer of ice on top of tundra lakes

details.summary: Tundra is a treeless biome found in Arctic regions and high mountains, characterized by permafrost, extreme cold, and a short growing season. Despite harsh conditions, tundra supports hardy mosses, lichens, and grasses along with adapted animals like caribou and arctic foxes.
details.whyItMatters: Arctic tundra stores massive amounts of carbon in permafrost. As climate change thaws permafrost, this carbon could be released as methane and CO2, potentially accelerating warming in a dangerous feedback loop.
takeaways: Permafrost underlies most tundra keeping the ground frozen year-round
The tundra growing season lasts only 50 to 60 days per year
Thawing permafrost may release billions of tons of stored greenhouse gases

faq.question: What is permafrost and why does it matter?
faq.answer: Permafrost is ground that stays frozen for at least two consecutive years, often for thousands. It stores twice as much carbon as the atmosphere. As temperatures rise, thawing permafrost releases methane and CO2, potentially creating an irreversible warming feedback.

faq.question: How do animals survive tundra winters?
faq.answer: Many migrate south like caribou, or hibernate like arctic ground squirrels. Year-round residents like arctic foxes grow thick winter coats and reduce heat loss through compact body shapes. Lemmings survive under insulating snow cover throughout winter.
